_comment: The rename map for the built-in button migration (design note section 7), read by check-styled-part-has-setting.py --fix. Corrected against the framework database and the disk on 2026-11-20 (see `corrections`). `old` -> `new` renames the attribute everywhere in the block's directory (block.json, render.php and partials, view and editor JS) and in the shared includes it is read from; `old` == `new` with a `value` only reshapes the attribute in block.json and lists every code read for review. `value.kind`: string-to-desktop-object, number-to-desktop-object, flat-box-to-desktop-object, true-to-full, fit-to-unset. `also_declared_by` names another block that declares the same name, so a shared include or a name scan must never touch that block (a whole-repo replace of ctaFontSize or ctaLineHeight would corrupt sgs/pricing-table). Saved post content still carries the old names: the same map is the input for the WP-CLI sweep of existing posts (no deprecated.js, FP-14).
corrections: ctaFontSize and ctaLineHeight are also declared by sgs/pricing-table (object); the note did not say so. Both entries carry also_declared_by so the pricing-table files and the shared includes that pricing-table reads are never rewritten by name.

The real readers of ctaFontSize and ctaLineHeight are prefixed reads inside includes/helpers-button-style.php::sgs_button_element_style_css ($read('FontSize') through absint(), $read('LineHeight') through sgs_button_element_line_height() which returns '' for an array), called with prefix 'cta' from product-card/render.php and includes/product-card-builtin-render.php. A name scan cannot see them. Once the attributes are objects, absint( array ) returns 1 (a 1px font) and the line height is dropped: the kit's design (section 3, step 2) must strip the typography keys from the look attributes and print them through sgs_typography_css_rule, or the migration breaks the card's CTA.

addToCartMinHeight, ctaFontSize and ctaLineHeight keep their names (the kit's bases are MinHeight, FontSize and LineHeight): they are shape changes, not renames. The note's wording was right; the map records them as reshape-only so --fix never renames them.
loginButtonFullWidth becomes loginButtonWidthType (kit base WidthType, enum fit/full), a boolean-to-string reshape; the note listed it correctly, with true -> full and false -> unset.
registerButton* has no look attributes today beyond registerButtonPreset and the registerButtonIcon* set, so the register button gains the whole kit through the generator; only the preset is renamed.
No new name collides: none of the new names exists in block_attributes today.

The kit stores padding and radius per device ({desktop,tablet,mobile} of sides or corners; registry value_shape device_sides and device_corners) and the border width as one box of sides. A block that stores a padding or a radius as one flat box (buybox addToCartPadding, product-card ctaPadding and ctaBorderRadius, choice-flow backBorderRadius) is reshaped with kind flat-box-to-desktop-object: the generator refuses the attribute until it is. The border widths (product-card ctaBorderWidth, choice-flow backBorderWidth) are flat sides already and need no row. account loginButtonPadding, loginButtonBorderRadius and loginButtonBorderWidth already match; their blocks state no default, so the generator lists them as kept with an unstated shape.

The default goes (a kit attribute has none) and a saved fit is dropped, so every card keeps its look and fit becomes a choice that does something
